# Awesome Loop

> Looped and recurrent-depth language models. Each deep card records the loop layout, what the main comparison holds fixed, the paper's results with table or figure references, and caveats taken from the paper. All numbers are author-reported; nothing is converted or extrapolated. Comparison keys: params = unique parameters, active-params = active parameters, flops = training FLOPs, kv = KV cache per token, tokens = training tokens, depth = executed layers per token, wallclock = wall-clock time.

## Deep cards

- [GLM-5.4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/zai-glm-5-4.md): Z.ai turns 28 layers of its pre-trained GLM-5 base into a two-pass loop through continued training at the 750B scale, with per-token gates, a shared-plus-sliding-window KV cache and reused sparse-attention indices. Layout: earlier layers (layer count not stated) -> [28 shared layers (28 layers)] x 2 -> later layers (layer count not stated); injection gated; KV first-pass. Held fixed: params; differs: flops.
- [Inkling 2 Mini](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/tml-inkling-2-mini.md): Open-weight MoE (26.4B total, 3.4B active) that runs the middle 12 of its 24 layers three times with shared weights, released with a variable-loop research twin used to measure how pass count affects capability and CoT monitorability. Layout: L0-5 (6 layers) -> [L6-17 (12 layers)] x 3 -> L18-23 (6 layers); injection depth-attention; KV per-pass. Held fixed: flops; differs: none.
- [Looped CED](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2611.13378.md): Loop the CED encoder layers that produce global KV, train with random depth, and keep only the last round's KV. Layout: L0-1 (2 layers) -> [L2-5 (4 layers)] x max(1, Poisson(8)) -> L6-11 (6 layers); injection gated; KV last-pass. Held fixed: params, tokens, kv; differs: flops, depth.
- [LoopDuet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2611.07211.md): Serve looped Transformers with fewer core loops for ordinary prompt tokens than for the last prompt token and the decoded tokens, run the deep tail as a compact batch in vLLM, and lower prefilling depth when the queue grows. Layout: prelude 4 layers -> [core 6 layers] x 32 (OLMo r32 checkpoint) -> coda 4 layers; injection n/a; KV last-pass. Held fixed: params, tokens, kv; differs: depth, wallclock.
- [SMELT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2609.01343.md): With per-token FLOPs, total parameters and KV cache matched, looping the middle half of an MoE Transformer twice lowers loss at four scales up to 54B non-embedding parameters and saves 6.8-18.0% of training FLOPs on the fitted frontier. Layout: L1-3 (3 layers) -> [L4-9 (6 layers)] x 2 -> L10-12 (3 layers); injection none; KV per-pass. Held fixed: flops, params, kv, tokens; differs: active-params, depth.
- [Parcae](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2604.12946.md): Constrain the loop's injection to a stable negative-diagonal form, sample depth per sequence, and fit training and test-time scaling laws for looping at fixed parameter count. Layout: prelude 8 layers -> [core 8 layers] x Poisson with mean 8, per sequence -> coda 8 layers; injection gated; KV n/a. Held fixed: params, tokens; differs: flops, depth.
- [YOCO-U](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2604.01220.md): Loop only YOCO's self-decoder, whose layers use sliding-window attention, so extra depth costs compute while the cross-decoder's global KV is still computed once. Layout: [Universal Self-Decoder, SWA-512 (10 layers)] x 3 -> Cross-Decoder, shared global KV (10 layers); injection none; KV single-global. Held fixed: params, active-params, flops; differs: tokens, depth, kv.
- [Retrofitted Recurrence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2511.07384.md): Turn pretrained 1B models into prelude-core-coda recurrent models by dropping middle layers and looping a block, then keep training while a curriculum raises the mean recurrence. Layout: L0-3 (4 layers) -> [L10-17 (8 layers)] x Poisson-Lognormal, mean ramped to 4, 8, 16 or 32 -> L18-21 (4 layers); injection concat; KV n/a. Held fixed: tokens; differs: params, flops, depth.
- [Ouro (LoopLM)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2510.25741.md): Pre-train a weight-tied layer stack that repeats 4 times, with a learned exit gate, on 7.7T tokens; the authors report that the 1.4B and 2.6B models match dense models of up to 12B parameters. Layout: [whole stack (2.6B: 48 layers) (24 layers)] x 8 in Stage 1a, then 4; injection none; KV per-pass. Held fixed: none; differs: params, tokens.
- [PLT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2510.24824.md): Run loop l of token i in the same forward pass as loop l+1 of token i-1, let later loops reuse the first loop's KV plus a gated SWA, and a looped model decodes at close to unlooped latency and KV. Layout: [all layers, every loop (100% of layers)] x 2 or 3 (PLT-2 / PLT-3); injection additive; KV first-pass. Held fixed: params, active-params, tokens; differs: flops, depth, kv.
- [MoR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2507.10524.md): Routers give each token its own number of passes through a shared middle block, and each pass caches KV only for its active tokens; at equal training FLOPs MoR beats fixed-depth recursive baselines and often vanilla, with fewer parameters. Layout: first layer (1 layer) -> [shared block (10 layers)] x 1-3 per token, set by the router (Nr=3) -> last layer (1 layer); injection none; KV per-pass. Held fixed: flops; differs: params, tokens, depth, kv.
- [Huginn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2502.05171.md): Pretrain a 3.5B prelude-core-coda transformer with a randomly sampled number of core iterations, so test-time compute scales by iterating the core more. Layout: P (2 layers) -> [R (4 layers)] x log-normal Poisson, mean 32 -> C (2 layers); injection concat; KV per-pass. Held fixed: params, tokens; differs: flops, depth.

## Other papers

- [Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27962): Puts learnable scalar gates on every sublayer of standard and looped Transformers so training removes the unneeded ones; carved models reach lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-11-20.
- [GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26509): Converts Qwen hybrid LMs into single-pass decision models via bidirectional full attention and multi-teacher distillation; checkpoint averaging plus parameter-free recurrent depth (reapplying middle layers) raises the 27B hidden-set score from 71.52 to 73.37. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-19.
- [dLoop: Looped Diffusion Language Models via Recurrent Latent Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26275): Restructures a pretrained diffusion language model into a Prelude-Loop-Coda design that reapplies a shared middle block before tokens are committed, reaching the highest or tied-highest accuracy on GSM8K, MATH, MBPP and HumanEval. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-19.
- [LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25595): LoopedWAM loops a shared six-block core in each expert of a robot world action model, and elastic self-distillation lets one checkpoint serve several action-depth and sampling-step budgets; it reaches 96.1% success on LIBERO. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-19.
- [Fold the Loop: Decoding-Time KV Memory for Looped Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25369): FoldCache lets groups of recurrent steps in a looped VLM share the group's final visual KV during decoding; on LoopVL it approximately halves prefix KV memory while matching full-cache accuracy on five open-ended benchmarks. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-19.
- [Late Entry in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24576): Late entry lets new tokens in looped language models skip early passes and run only the final passes over a deep context cache, outperforming matched early exit; Wake verification reaches 5.2x greedy-exact speedup on Ouro-2.6B. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-18.
- [LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24301): Proposes LoopCache, self-speculative decoding for long-context looped Transformers that updates drafts across intermediate loops by confidence and rotates loop-specific KV caches; reports average 10.25x and 14.56x speedup over WFD and LoopSpec. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-18.
- [Simpler Tiny Recursive Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23677): STRM simplifies TRM to a single uniformly updated state, using jittered-rate exponential moving updates and slow-channel readout; under TRM's data, parameters and compute it gains 3.8 points on Sudoku-Extreme and matches TRM on Maze-Hard. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-18.
- [Proximal Targets: Training Looped Refiners on Problems with Many Correct Answers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22737): Proves that a single stored target sets a loss floor for looped refiners (HRM, TRM) on puzzles with many answers; training each pass toward the nearest correct answer solves 98.8% of multi-answer Sudoku versus 2.5%. Category: applications; focus: core; 2026-11-17.
- [LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22728): LoopZip compresses visual tokens in looped vision-language models without training, selecting tokens by attention from two calls of the same shared layer; on LoopVL-1B it keeps 97.16% of the original performance at 50% pruning ratio. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-17.
- [InfuseLoop: Cross-Trajectory Latent Injection for Scalable Parallel Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22426): Adds cross-trajectory latent injection to Parallel Looped Transformers, so each loop aggregates causally available hidden states from later trajectories via attention residuals; this eliminates training-loss spikes and improves validation-loss scaling up to eight loops. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-17.
- [Latent Fact Composition under Next-Token Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21921): Baton looped transformers pass the intermediate entity to the second loop as a token embedding; trained only on answers, two variants almost solve held-out two-hop questions, but next-token training makes accuracy rise then decline. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-11-16.
- [Déjà-Events: Multi-view 3D Geometry with Event Cameras via Sparsity-Aware Adaptive Gating](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21302): Distils an event-camera 3D model from the RGB teacher Déjà View, which repeatedly applies one shared transformer block, and gates that block by event density; it has the lowest pointmap error among evaluated event-based methods. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-16.
- [Efficient Multi-View Generation with Iterative Global-Local Proxy Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20703): GLPA sends cross-view information in multi-view diffusion through compact proxies and refines them by reusing the same attention parameters within a denoising step; on FLUX, attention runs 2.65× faster than dense attention and reconstruction improves. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-16.
- [Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20404): Tests latent feedback, which feeds each token's top-layer state into the next token's input, against compute-matched multi-epoch Transformers; it saves at most 48% of the compute and 47% of the unique data. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-11-16.
- [LoopSkim: Lossless Multi-Depth Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19896): Proposes lossless speculative decoding for looped LMs in which each loop's readout checks draft tokens copied from the context and only full-depth readouts commit; without training, its speedup averages 1.73x that of LoopSpec. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-15.
- [When Does Reusing Layers Help Multimodal Embeddings?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19827): Tests eleven loop designs for multimodal embeddings, proving that under forward-only attention repeated layers cannot make earlier image states query-dependent; on MMEB-V2 an added loop loses 0.46 points, while native recurrence gains +4.23 points. Category: understanding; focus: related; 2026-11-15.
- [LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19649): A training-free speculative decoding method for looped LLMs that puts multi-token suffix drafts and shallow-loop predictions in one draft tree; average speedup over greedy decoding is 5.85x on Ouro-2.6B and 5.13x on Huginn-3.5B. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-14.
- [Architectures and KV Replay for Depth-Recurrent Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19446): Studies how to cut decoding KV memory in depth-recurrent LMs: looped hybrids need frequent attention anchors, and training with recurrent KV replay lets iterations share KV states with performance close to separate per-iteration caches. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-14.
- [Wireless Edge-Assisted Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Physical AI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19131): Uses constrained deep RL (TRPO-Lag) to jointly choose local or edge execution and the latent-reasoning convergence threshold of a recurrent-depth VLA, reaching up to 23% higher feasibility-weighted task success than benchmark constrained RL methods. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-14.
- [Folding Language Models into Themselves](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18113): Concertina folds every N adjacent teacher layers into one shared block run N times with low-rank corrections; distilled from Qwen3-4B on 22B tokens, a 2.27B model retains 84% of the teacher averaged over eight benchmarks. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-13.
- [Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17309): CRAM, a learned Hopfield-Tank energy minimized at inference, solves 99.996% of Sudoku-Extreme and 100% of Maze-Unique test puzzles with training at least 1,000x faster than looped models; the authors call these benchmarks trivially solvable. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-12.
- [Rectified Looped Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16265): Feeds each loop a linear interpolation between the current state and the block's prediction; at matched depth this lowers perplexity versus a standard looped Transformer and keeps hidden-state norms more stable, with no extra parameters. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-12.
- [One Block Is Enough: LoopMR for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14947): Reuses one Restormer block at every iteration of unrolled MRI reconstruction and beats PromptMR+ with about 1/9 of its parameters; shared transformer blocks match or beat distinct-weight ones, while shared CNN blocks do worse. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-11.
- [Depth as a Candidate Source: Portfolio Allocation for Recurrent Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12293): Shows deeper recurrence in a frozen Huginn can lose correct answers found at shallower depths, and proposes Depth Portfolio Allocation, which spreads a test-time budget across depths and expands oracle coverage at matched candidate counts. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-11-09.
- [WiFo-R: Wireless Foundation Model with Recurrent Channel Representation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11275): Builds a wireless channel foundation model whose parameter-shared recurrent updates refine CSI features and add latent tokens; multi-depth pretraining trains intermediate states to reconstruct CSI, and selectable depth improves the accuracy-complexity trade-off. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-08.
- [Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08977): Learns an energy over latent reasoning states and makes each loop a gradient step on it, giving a stopping signal; reaches 99.9% accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme with 345× less inference compute than the next-best model. Category: applications; focus: core; 2026-11-06.
- [ARC-VLN: Adaptive Recursive Computing-based Visual-Language Navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18696): ARC-VLN runs a shared-parameter language backbone recursively for aerial VLN, letting only visual tokens exit early; on OpenFly it has the lowest navigation error of the compared methods and reduces FLOPs and GPU memory. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-05.
- [AlterNet: Adaptive-Depth Mixture-of-Experts with Learned Halting for Elastic Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08741): AlterNet loops over a shared pool of shallow MoE experts, picked by a depth-aware router, with per-expert halt heads for early stopping, so depth adapts and can be cut without retraining; results are preliminary. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-11-05.
- [Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08236): Replaces ViT self-attention with a separable sum-of-Gaussians operator, globally Lipschitz with fixed kernels, across discrete, looped and Neural ODE ViTs; in the looped setting it raises CIFAR-100 Top-1 accuracy by 5.4-8.1 points. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-05.
- [Extending Reasoning in Typed Decision Models via Looping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07736): RELOAD fine-tunes pretrained encoders or decoders with a damped loop over their middle block; looping improves accuracy and calibration, mostly on reasoning chains longer than in training, where encoders gain up to 23 points. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-05.
- [BRIDGE: Bridging the Semantic Quantization Gap for Generative Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07425): For generative recommendation, BRIDGE adds latent reasoning, self-distillation and effort-aware recurrence, which runs a shared loop decoder more times at early Semantic ID levels; it improves Recall@10 and NDCG@10 on three Amazon benchmarks. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-05.
- [Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07226): Loopback Transformer reads each shared-block update separately, using geometric decay for total update weight and attention to allocate it; it reaches lower validation loss than standard Transformers with 40-75% of their Transformer parameters. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-04.
- [LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Causal Encoder-Decoder Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06835): Loops the decoder layers of a causal encoder-decoder, storing each token's KV only on its first visit; one model covers 3 to 21 layer executions per token and, with enough loops, beats a single-pass baseline. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-11-04.
- [Loop Before You Leap: What Recurrent Depth Can and Cannot Buy in Data-Limited Pretraining](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06206): Compares standard and looped Transformers under a 100M-word budget; text-only, a 12-layer stack repeated four times beats a 48-layer Transformer by 5.4 BLiMP points, but recurrence does not clearly mitigate the multimodal-training drop. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-11-04.
- [Give the Drafter a Second Chance to Guess: Parallel Reconsideration for Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05724): Lets a speculative-decoding drafter deepen uncertain guesses with extra passes of its shared block, run in parallel with the one-pass draft; this improves acceptance length by 5.3% to 10.2% and speedup by 3.5% to 9.2%. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-03.
- [LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05304): LoopVQ vector-quantizes the KV cache of looped transformers, coding channels of several loop steps jointly; with Ouro and Huginn at 0.5 bits per element, it outperforms KV vector quantization methods built for standard LLMs. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-03.
- [ARLoop: Fully-Open Pre-trained Looped Transformers with Attention Residuals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05234): ARLoop gives each layer of a looped transformer attention over earlier outputs across depth; sliding-window depth attention matches full history, and a 1.2B model trained on 0.5T tokens beats Huginn-3.5B on all evaluated tasks. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-03.
- [What Sets the Serving Speed of Looped Language Models? Measurements and Optimizations Graded by Exactness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05150): Measures serving of looped LMs Ouro and Huginn-0125, grading optimizations by exactness; the many small kernels per token set the cost, and fusing them behind rounding fences raises throughput 1.11-1.59x with identical outputs. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-03.
- [Best-of-Depth: Learning Exploratory Dynamics in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04663): Best-of-Depth trains a looped Transformer's recurrent trajectory as a candidate set by minimizing prediction loss across depths; on N-Queens, coverage reaches 91.03% versus 45.75% for final-depth training. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-03.
- [LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04137): Chooses 4-bit, 2-bit or final-loop KV reuse for each (loop, layer) cell of Ouro from an offline profile; serving Ouro-1.4B, the LoopKV-M plan stores 35% less KV than KIVI-4 and sustains 1.7-2.2x its goodput. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-03.
- [Dory1.0-4B: A Looped Normalized-GPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03998): Dory1.0-4B is a looped nGPT language model with elastic depth, pre-trained on 6 trillion tokens; more loops raise accuracy, and caching only last-loop KV keeps most gains at a non-looped KV footprint. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-11-02.
- [Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03526): Library of Layers uses a router to choose and order blocks from a global library at inference, covering dense, depth-recurrent and MoE designs; it is competitive with all three when pretrained on text. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-11-02.
- [Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02857): Trains a looped transformer whose update operator, independent of the iteration count, keeps refining multi-view geometry from its current state, so one solver handles offline and incremental reconstruction, relocalization and streaming without task-specific training. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-02.
- [When Does Adaptive Halting Win? Selection Rules Matter in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02333): On a frozen Ouro-1.4B, pre-registered tests show the winner between a trained stability probe and Ouro's exit gate flips with the operating-point selection rule; the probe shows no demonstrated advantage over an untrained KL baseline. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-11-02.
- [How Does Chain-of-Thought Supervision Teach Models to Reason? A Theoretical Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01740): Studies an in-context linear-regression weight predictor trained on gradient-descent trajectories and run recursively beyond them; long-horizon reasoning has phase transitions in context length and training CoT budget, and overthinking splits into error accumulation and amplification. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-11-01.
- [There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.42030): Adds loops to pretrained Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models (0.8B to 9B) and compares them with equal-parameter and equal-FLOPs unlooped baselines; only the looped 0.8B model beats both, so post-pretraining loops pay only for small models. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-10-30.
- [Where KV-Cache Error Lives in Looped Language Models: A Diagnostic Study of Ouro and Huginn](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41825): Studies how KV and shared-weight quantization error changes next-token distributions in looped LMs Ouro and Huginn-0125; per unit of error, values carry 94% of diagonal Fisher mass, but keys dominate measured KL. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-30.
- [ElTab: Elastically Looped Tabular Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41819): ElTab trains one looped tabular transformer with supervision at randomly sampled early exits; on 30 OpenML datasets it matches six depth-specific looped models and a 12-layer TabPFN-style baseline with 25% fewer inference FLOPs. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-30.
- [UpLoop: Training Looped Transformers via Upcycling at No Extra Pretraining Compute](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41720): Grows a shallow Transformer by copying layers and spends the saved compute on looping a shared middle block, at matched parameters, tokens and FLOPs; the 1.3B model's 22-task average rises from 22.99 to 27.52. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-30.
- [How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40325): In looped decoders up to 1B parameters, full-stack looping is best at fixed parameters and middle-block looping at fixed training FLOPs; per-loop low-rank adapters help, and a normalization fix recovers Parallel Loop Transformer quality. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-10-29.
- [CopyLoop: Fast Looped Transformer Decoding via Context Copying and Shallow Screening](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38822): CopyLoop, a training-free decoding algorithm for looped Transformers, proposes multi-token suffixes from repeated context, screens them at shallow recurrent depth and verifies at full depth, reaching 2.98x--10.70x speedups on Base models. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-28.
- [Deeper Backpropagation or More Updates? Training Looped Language Models Across Budgets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38422): Compares shorter and longer truncated-backprop windows for training looped language models at roughly equal training time; the advantage of shorter windows shrinks as training budgets grow, so the preferred window can change. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-28.
- [Compute Has Shape: Self-Morphing the Internal Computation of Frozen LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38382): SelfMorph trains a selector that picks, per input, whether a frozen LLM keeps its forward path, repeats a layer span or branches hidden states; this gives an 8.06% mean relative improvement on five in-distribution benchmarks. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-10-28.
- [Think Twice: The Metis-1.6 Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37903): Metis-1.6 technical report on Praxis and Logos, two from-scratch models that run a hybrid Mamba-2 and attention MoE stack twice per token; Logos averages 52.93 across 40 post-trained benchmarks, and the report documents training failures. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-27.
- [LoopFold: Parallelizing Recurrent Depth in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35556): LoopFold runs several recurrent depths of a looped Transformer in parallel batches, using a predictor for later-loop inputs and a corrector for their outputs; versus a nine-loop vanilla model it cuts decoding latency by 46%. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-26.
- [StateLoop: Persistent State for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35544): StateLoop gives each token a gated persistent state carried across looped-Transformer iterations and projected back into the backbone output; it lowers Pile perplexity versus vanilla looping, with a gap that grows with trained loop depth. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-10-26.
- [Cross-Loop Query Handoff: How Later Loops Redirect Two-Hop Retrieval in the Ouro Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34639): Transplants attention queries between loops of Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B; loop-3 queries injected into loop 1 rescue 90% and 97% of synthetic two-hop loop-1 failures that loop 3 fixes, versus 24% and 21% with shuffled donors. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-10-25.
- [Recursive CLIP: Vision-Language Distillation with Looped Transformer Blocks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34563): Trains and distills CLIP models with recursive encoders that apply N transformer blocks M times at fixed ViT-B depth; CLIP tolerates substantial recurrent block reuse, though the effect depends on the encoder and downstream task. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-25.
- [Recency Is the Wrong Axis: A Negative Result on Windowed Deepest-Plane KV Caching in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34436): Tests a KV policy for looped models that keeps every loop's plane for recent positions and shares the deepest plane elsewhere; across three models, sharing cost depends on late-loop convergence and position, not recency. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-25.
- [ScaleRLT: Exact Log-Probabilities and Fast Deferred Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning on Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34427): ScaleRLT removes the log-probability mismatch between deferred rollouts and the learner's dense pass in RL on looped transformers, using a stop-gradient hybrid that replays the rollout schedule bit for bit and keeps the dense gradient. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-25.
- [LoopGR: Parameter-Efficient Scaling for Generative Recommendation via Recurrent Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34157): For generative recommendation, LoopGR alternates a shared generative decoder with a lightweight context updater over recurrent depth and self-distills a low-budget student; it beats an encoder-decoder baseline while reducing model size by up to 52%. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-25.
- [One Model, Two Paths: Balancing Single-Pass and Looped Performance in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33517): Adapts a pretrained model to support both single-pass and looped inference by reusing middle-layer weights, and shows joint weighted losses with frozen-model guidance reduce single-pass degradation while keeping looped gains over continued training. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-24.
- [Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23036): Isolates loop placement, input injection and recurrent-state design in matched from-scratch looped LMs; a prelude-recurrent-coda Huginn-style design outperforms Ouro across all ten benchmarks at 730M parameters and 336B tokens, and the advantage transfers to MoE. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-10-16.
- [Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06833): Shows that near fixed points looped LMs can skip recurrence paths in training, decoding, prefill and RL; its learned depth prior and orthogonal input injection lower perplexity over existing choices from 100M to 1.6B. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-05.
- [FlashLoop: Fast and Memory-Efficient Looped Transformers via Lazy Updates](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29812): FlashLoop, a training-free inference framework, cuts cross-loop redundancy in looped Transformers with token-sparse updates, sparse attention and KV-residual quantization, giving up to 1.64x speedup and 6x less KV-cache memory while largely preserving accuracy. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-24.
- [WaveFront Decoding: Parallelized Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23033): Wavefront Decoding is a training-free self-speculative decoder for looped language models that co-batches shallow drafting and full-depth verification in the same recurrent-block calls, reaching 2.42x speedup on Ouro-2.6B and 3.54x on Huginn-3.5B over autoregressive decoding. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-19.
- [LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184): LoopSpec, a training-free self-speculative decoder for looped Transformers, drafts tokens from early recurrent states and overlaps drafting with verification; it stays lossless under greedy and sampling decoding and reaches up to 6.83× speedup. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-15.
- [Thinking with Looped Flows](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11801): Trains looped models with local denoising objectives at decreasing noise levels and infers by integrating a probability flow; across six reasoning benchmarks it outperforms prior looped models overall, reaching 58.8% test accuracy on ARC-AGI-1. Category: applications; focus: core; 2026-09-10.
- [RecurTrace: Adaptive Latent Reasoning with Loop-Time Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03379): Loops a middle block of an LM, adding attention over earlier loop states and an oracle-supervised halting head; on MathQA it reaches 56.9% with 2.0 loops on average, 2.2 points above the best fixed depth. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-09-03.
- [Looped Transformers under the Jacobian Lens: Does the Global Workspace Survive Recurrence?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01924): Applies an extended Jacobian lens to Ouro-2.6B and Huginn-0125: both form a workspace in their iterated part, but Ouro rebuilds content every loop, while Huginn carries it forward and interventions act within about two recurrences. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-09-01.
- [Think Shallow, Solve Deep: Controlling Recurrent Dynamics for Reliable Test-Time Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18222): Shows that a trained recurrent operator's dynamical regime (settling, marginal or drifting) predicts whether extra test-time iterations help, preserve or degrade answers on algorithmic tasks; a terminal fixed-point objective controls the regime. Category: applications; focus: core; 2026-08-18.
- [Recirculation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17981): Recirculation feeds part of a deep layer activation into a shallow layer of frozen pretrained transformers, adding recurrence over depth and tokens; adaptive recirculation on Gemma3 lowers perplexity and raises relative GSM8k accuracy by 21%. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-08-18.
- [Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09444): Continuous depth batching forms new batches between loop steps so looped LMs can serve tokens exiting at different depths; on Ouro 1.4B and Huginn 3.5B it realizes up to 99% of the estimated maximum speedup. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-08-10.
- [Full-bandwidth transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08888): Fuses each step's top-layer state with the sampled token embedding through a gate and feeds it back as the next input; 1B models match or approach standard transformers trained on roughly 1.5x more tokens. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-08-09.
- [Retrofitting Recurrent Depth into a Pretrained Language Model: Installation, Extrapolation, Transfer, and Retention at Two Parameter Budgets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11233): Splits Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct into prelude, weight-tied recurrent block and coda; with intermediate-step supervision it computes one task step per loop, extrapolates to roughly 1.5 times its supervised depth, and beats a scratchpad model 84% versus 72%. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-07-31.
- [Nanbeige4.2-3B: Unlocking Agentic Capabilities in a Compact Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22083): Nanbeige4.2-3B is pretrained from scratch on 28T tokens as a Looped Transformer that reuses its layer stack, then post-trained with SFT and RL; it outperforms larger models including Qwen3.5-9B and Gemma4-12B on agentic benchmarks. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-07-24.
- [When Does Recurrence Become an Algorithm? Convergence Selection in Weight-Tied Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20594): Trains weight-tied looped transformers on group word problems; training installs a serial frontier that solves about n_train/T_train positions per loop, and weight tying, not expressivity, selects it over the parallel scans untied models learn. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-07-22.
- [Loop the Loopies!](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16051): Loopie comprises two open-source looped MoE Transformers (20B with 2B active, 6B with 0.6B active) that repeat each layer in place; ablations show they outperform vanilla Transformers trained with the same compute budget. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-07-17.
- [Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15456): Looped Latent Attention, a post-training codec, stores the per-loop KV cache as compact latents and rebuilds loop-specific K/V on read; at matched cache budget it beats head-axis MLA, cross-layer sharing, KV quantization and final-loop reuse. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-07-16.
- [T^2MLR: Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15178): T2MLR fuses a middle-layer state cached from the previous token into an earlier layer at the current token; it beats data- and parameter-matched Transformers, and recurrence over a middle block often beats full-layer recurrence. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-07-16.
- [DeepLoop: Depth Scaling for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13491): DeepLoop derives a residual-scaling rule for looped Transformers that counts repeated visits to shared blocks; in GPT-2 small and medium looped language models it improves validation loss and downstream accuracy once blocks are revisited. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-07-15.
- [Adaptive Depth in Looped Transformers: Diagnosing Learned Halting Gates and Trajectory Readouts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20519): Splits adaptive depth in looped Transformers into trajectory formation and exit readout; fixed-prior depth supervision plus confidence readouts often matches or beats learned halting gates, and Ouro's pretrained gates are competitive but not uniformly Pareto-optimal. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-07-08.
- [DiscoLoop: Looping Discrete Embeddings and Continuous Hidden States for Multi-hop Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00341): Finds that a looped transformer's first loop leaves the two-hop bridge entity decodable but misaligned with its embedding; DiscoLoop adds a decoded-embedding channel between loops and outperforms looped baselines on multi-hop tasks and in pretraining. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-07-01.
- [Bridging the Gap Between Latent and Explicit Reasoning with Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31779): LOTUS loops a pretrained LM over padded latent blocks and supervises each latent position with its gold CoT-step token; at 3B scale it closes the gap to explicit CoT while cutting thought-phase latency 2.5x-6.9x. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-06-30.
- [Fixed-Point Reasoners: Stable and Adaptive Deep Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18206): FPRM stabilizes deep looped Transformers with pre-norm layers and residual scaling and halts when the hidden state reaches a fixed point, adapting compute to task difficulty; it is effective on Sudoku, Maze, state-tracking and ARC-AGI. Category: applications; focus: core; 2026-06-16.
- [LoopCoder-v2: Only Loop Once for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18023): LoopCoder-v2 trains 7B Parallel Loop Transformer coders on 18T tokens; two loops lift SWE-bench Verified from 43.0 (non-looped) to 64.4, but three or more regress as later-loop gains shrink against a roughly fixed position-offset cost. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-06-16.
- [Skip a Layer or Loop It? Learning Program-of-Layers in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06574): Shows that frozen pretrained LLMs admit per-input programs that skip or repeat layer segments, and trains a lightweight predictor of such programs that improves math reasoning accuracy over standard inference, often using fewer layers. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-06-04.
- [LoopMoE: Unifying Iterative Computation with Mixture-of-Experts for Language Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04438): LoopMoE loops an MoE block with iteration- and token-conditioned normalization (IterAdaLN); over a vanilla MoE with identical parameters and FLOPs, its average gain grows from over 1 point at 3B to approximately 3 at 9B. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-06-03.
- [Déjà View: Looping Transformers for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30215): DéjàView applies a single looped transformer block to per-view features for K refinement steps in multi-view 3D reconstruction; it matches or beats much larger feed-forward models on five benchmarks and beats an untied per-step variant. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-28.
- [Latent Recurrent Transformer: Architecture Exploration, Training Strategies, and Scaling Behavior](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26797): LRT feeds the previous token's high-level hidden state into the next token's layers; at matched effective compute it improves BPB and CORE and matches a three-loop Transformer in BPB, with one forward per token. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-05-26.
- [Stabilizing Recurrent Dynamics for Test-Time Scalable Latent Reasoning in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26733): STARS trains looped LMs with Jacobian spectral radius regularization and random loop sampling so latent states approach stable fixed points, giving reliable test-time scaling on arithmetic and less degradation with deeper recurrence in math reasoning. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-05-26.
- [Training-Free Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23872): Loops a contiguous mid-stack block of a frozen checkpoint at inference without training; naive reapplication usually hurts, but damped sub-steps of the block's ODE update help, e.g. +2.64 pp MMLU-Pro on Qwen3-4B-Instruct. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-05-22.
- [Equilibrium Reasoners: Learning Attractors Enables Scalable Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21488): Equilibrium Reasoners frame iterative latent reasoning as learning task-conditioned attractors and scale depth and breadth at test time; gains track convergence to solution attractors, reaching over 99% on Sudoku-Extreme versus 2.6% for feedforward models. Category: applications; focus: core; 2026-05-20.
- [LT2: Linear-Time Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20670): LT2 replaces softmax attention in looped transformers with linear or sparse attention; looping refines linear-attention memory and widens the sparse receptive field, and hybrid variants match or surpass the standard looped transformer at lower cost. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-05-20.
- [HRM-Text: Efficient Pretraining Beyond Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20613): HRM-Text pretrains a hierarchical recurrent language model with MagicNorm, warmup deep credit assignment and a task-completion objective on instruction-response pairs; a 1B model on 40 billion unique tokens performs competitively with 2-7B open models. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-05-20.
- [Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19943): PTRM injects Gaussian noise at each deep recursion step of a trained TRM to run parallel trajectories and selects among them with its Q head; without retraining, Sudoku-Extreme accuracy rises from 87.4% to 98.75%. Category: applications; focus: core; 2026-05-19.
- [Generative Recursive Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19376): GRAM makes recursive reasoning models stochastic latent-variable generative models trained by amortized variational inference, scaling inference by recursion depth and parallel trajectory sampling; it beats deterministic recursive baselines on structured and multi-solution reasoning. Category: applications; focus: core; 2026-05-19.
- [Solve the Loop: Attractor Models for Language and Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12466): Attractor Models refine a backbone's output embedding by solving for a fixed point with implicit gradients, keeping training memory constant; a 770M model outperforms a 1.3B Transformer trained on twice as many tokens. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-05-12.
- [Simply Stabilizing the Loop via Fully Looped Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18797): Fully Looped Transformer injects the previous loop's output into every layer by reusing self-attention, adding no parameters; it curbs residual explosion and gradient oscillation and trains stably up to 12 loop iterations, where baselines collapse. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-05-11.
- [LoopUS: Recasting Pretrained LLMs into Looped Latent Refinement Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11011): LoopUS splits a pretrained LLM into encoder, looped reasoning block and decoder, adding a selective gate, random deep supervision and a confidence head for early exit; this improves reasoning-oriented performance without recurrent training from scratch. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-05-10.
- [Sparse Layers are Critical to Scaling Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09165): Compares dense and MoE transformers with and without looping; Looped-MoE out-scales the standard baseline while dense looped models do not, since routing picks different experts per pass, and loop boundaries are better early-exit points. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-05-09.
- [Memory-Efficient Looped Transformer: Decoupling Compute from Memory in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07721): MELT, fine-tuned from Ouro, keeps one KV cache per layer that is shared across loops and updated by a learned gate; it outperforms comparable-size LLMs with a similar memory footprint, far smaller than Ouro's. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-05-08.
- [Universal Transformers Need Memory: Depth-State Trade-offs in Adaptive Recursive Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21999): Studies learned memory tokens in a single-block Universal Transformer with ACT on Sudoku-Extreme; without them no configuration reaches non-trivial accuracy, and inverting the halting-router bias to -3 avoids an initialization trap that breaks most runs. Category: applications; focus: core; 2026-04-23.
- [Hyperloop Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21254): Hyperloop Transformers loop the middle block and add loop-level hyper-connections with matrix-valued residual streams; across scales they compare well with depth-matched Transformer and mHC baselines while using approximately 50% fewer parameters. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-04-23.
- [How Much Is One Recurrence Worth? Iso-Depth Scaling Laws for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21106): Fits a joint scaling law over an iso-depth pretraining sweep of looped language models and measures a recurrence-equivalence exponent of 0.46, so replacing unique blocks with shared recurrences raises validation loss at matched training compute. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-04-22.
- [Stability and Generalization in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15259): A fixed-point analysis of looped transformers proves that models without recall cannot achieve strong input-dependence, while recall with outer normalization yields stable, input-dependent fixed points; small models on chess, sudoku and prefix-sums follow these predictions. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-04-16.
- [A Mechanistic Analysis of Looped Reasoning Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.11791): Analyzes latent states of pretrained looped language models; in many, each recurrent-block layer converges to a distinct fixed point and each iteration repeats feedforward-like stages of inference, depending on input injection and normalization. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-04-13.
- [ELT: Elastic Looped Transformers for Visual Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.09168): ELT loops weight-shared transformer blocks for image and video generation and distills the maximum-loop output into intermediate loops for any-time inference; with 4× fewer parameters at iso-inference compute, it reaches FID 2.0 on ImageNet 256×256. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-04-10.
- [Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07822): Trains recurrent-depth Transformers from scratch on implicit multi-hop knowledge composition; unlike vanilla Transformers they generalize systematically through a three-stage grokking process and extrapolate to deeper compositions with more inference-time iterations, until overthinking degrades predictions. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-04-09.
- [Adaptive Loops and Memory in Transformers: Think Harder or Know More?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08391): Lets each block loop with learned halting and adds gated memory banks; looping mainly helps math, memory banks help commonsense tasks, and combined they beat an iso-FLOP baseline with three times the layers on math. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-03-09.
- [Mixture of Universal Experts: Scaling Virtual Width via Depth-Width Transformation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04971): MoUE reuses a shared pool of universal experts across MoE layers under a fixed activation budget; it beats matched MoE baselines by up to 1.3% and converts existing MoE checkpoints with up to 4.2% gains. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-03-05.
- [AdaPonderLM: Gated Pondering Language Models with Token-Wise Adaptive Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01914): AdaPonderLM, a recurrent LM, learns token-wise halting with iteration-specific MLP gates and reuses KV states of halted tokens; it cuts inference compute by about 10% at comparable perplexity, spending more compute on high-NLL tokens. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-03-02.
- [From Growing to Looping: A Unified View of Iterative Computation in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16490): Looped and depth-grown (middle-layer duplication) LLMs share depth-wise signatures of iterative computation; looping a middle block of a depth-grown model at inference, without loop training, raises accuracy on some reasoning primitives by up to 2x. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-02-18.
- [SpiralFormer: Looped Transformers Can Learn Hierarchical Dependencies via Multi-Resolution Recursion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11698): SpiralFormer runs a looped Transformer's shared core at a different sequence resolution each iteration, coarse to fine; from 160M to 1.4B it beats looped and non-looped baselines in parameter and compute efficiency. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-02-12.
- [LoopFormer: Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers for Latent Reasoning via Shortcut Modulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11451): Trains one looped Transformer for many depths via time and step-size conditioning and a shortcut-consistency loss; it performs well on language modeling and reasoning under tight compute budgets and improves as the budget grows. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-02-11.
- [Prioritize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Rewarding Latent Thought Trajectories Improves Reasoning in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10520): RLTT replaces GRPO's final-state credit with reward spread over the whole latent thought trajectory of looped LMs; on Ouro-Thinking it raises mean math accuracy over GRPO by +5.8% at 1.4B and +10.9% at 2.6B. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-02-11.
- [Looping Back to Move Forward: Recursive Transformers for Efficient and Flexible Large Multimodal Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09080): RecursiveVLM loops a multimodal model's LLM backbone, adding a Recursive Connector that fuses intermediate-layer states per modality and a Monotonic Recursion Loss; it gains +3% over standard Transformers and +7% over vanilla recursive baselines. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-02-09.
- [Recurrent-Depth VLA: Implicit Test-Time Compute Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models via Latent Iterative Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07845): RD-VLA gives a VLA a weight-tied recurrent action head that stops on latent convergence; tasks failing at one iteration exceed 90 percent success with four, and inference is up to 80x faster than reasoning VLAs. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-02-08.
- [LoopViT: Scaling Visual ARC with Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02156): Loop-ViT iterates a weight-tied hybrid convolution-attention block on ARC-AGI grids and at inference halts once predictive entropy is low; the 18M model reaches 65.8% on ARC-AGI-1, above 73M-parameter ensembles. Category: applications; focus: core; 2026-02-02.
- [Depth-Recurrent Attention Mixture (Dreamer): Giving Latent Reasoning the Attention it Deserves](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21582): Dreamer combines sequence attention, depth attention and sparse expert attention in a depth-recurrent model; against FLOP-, parameter- and memory-matched baselines it needs 2 to 8x fewer training tokens for the same accuracy on language reasoning. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-01-29.
- [Loop as a Bridge: Can Looped Transformers Truly Link Representation Space and Natural Language Outputs?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10242): Tests whether looping lets Ouro close the gap between internal representations and verbal outputs; more loops narrow it partly because representational knowledge degrades, and injected concepts are perceived only in the final loop. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-01-15.
- [Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04871): TRM, a single 2-layer network that recursively refines a latent state and an answer, generalizes better than HRM on puzzles; with 7M parameters it reaches 45% on ARC-AGI-1 and 8% on ARC-AGI-2. Category: applications; focus: core; 2025-10-06.
- [Energy-Based Transformers are Scalable Learners and Thinkers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02092): Energy-Based Transformers predict by gradient descent on a learned energy over input-prediction pairs; versus Transformer++, they show up to 35% higher training scaling rate and 29% more gain from System 2 Thinking on language tasks. Category: adjacent; focus: related; 2025-07-02.
- [Hierarchical Reasoning Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21734): HRM couples a slow high-level and a fast low-level recurrent module; with 27 million parameters and 1000 training samples, it nearly solves complex Sudoku and large mazes and beats larger models on ARC. Category: applications; focus: core; 2025-06-26.
- [PonderLM: Pretraining Language Models to Ponder in Continuous Space](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20674): PonderLM feeds the probability-weighted sum of token embeddings back into the same model for several forward passes per token, learned by self-supervised pretraining; PonderPythia-2.8B surpasses Pythia-6.9B and rivals Pythia-12B. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2025-05-27.
- [A Little Depth Goes a Long Way: The Expressive Power of Log-Depth Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.03961): Proves that looped transformers repeating middle layers Θ(log n) times recognize regular languages and solve graph connectivity, which fixed-depth transformers cannot under standard conjectures; growing depth is more efficient than growing width or chain-of-thought steps. Category: theory; focus: core; 2025-03-05.
- [CODI: Compressing Chain-of-Thought into Continuous Space via Self-Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.21074): CODI jointly trains explicit-CoT teacher and implicit-CoT student tasks, aligning a designated token's hidden states to compress CoT into continuous space; at GPT-2 scale it matches explicit CoT on GSM8k with 3.1x compression. Category: adjacent; focus: related; 2025-02-28.
- [Reasoning with Latent Thoughts: On the Power of Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17416): Shows that a k-layer transformer looped L times nearly matches a kL-layer model on synthetic reasoning and is competitive on language-model reasoning tasks, and proves T loops can simulate T steps of CoT. Category: theory; focus: core; 2025-02-24.
- [Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06769): Coconut feeds the last hidden state back as the next input embedding rather than decoding it into a token; these continuous thoughts can encode alternative next steps, and Coconut outperforms CoT on search-heavy logical reasoning. Category: adjacent; focus: related; 2024-12-09.
- [Relaxed Recursive Transformers: Effective Parameter Sharing with Layer-wise LoRA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20672): Converts pretrained LLMs into Recursive Transformers that loop one shared block, optionally relaxed with depth-wise LoRA; recursive Gemma 1B beats TinyLlama 1.1B, Pythia 1B and distillation baselines and recovers most of Gemma 2B's performance. Category: training; focus: core; 2024-10-28.
- [Can Looped Transformers Learn to Implement Multi-step Gradient Descent for In-context Learning?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08292): Proves that for in-context linear regression, the global minimizer of a linear looped Transformer's training loss implements multi-step preconditioned gradient descent, and that gradient flow converges fast despite non-convexity; synthetic experiments agree. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-10-10.
- [On Expressive Power of Looped Transformers: Theoretical Analysis and Enhancement via Timestep Encoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01405): Derives approximation rates for looped Transformers, revealing a limitation specific to looping, and adds per-loop scaling parameters conditioned on timestep encoding; in experiments more loops improve performance and timestep encoding adds further gains. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-10-02.
- [Looped Transformers for Length Generalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15647): Trains looped decoder-only Transformers on tasks with known iterative RASP-L solutions, supervising only the final answer after an input-dependent number of steps; adapting the step count at test time improves length generalization. Category: applications; focus: core; 2024-09-24.
- [MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16039): MoEUT is a shared-layer Transformer with mixture-of-experts feedforward and attention layers, layer grouping and peri-layernorm; it slightly outperforms standard Transformers on language modeling tasks such as BLiMP and PIQA using less compute and memory. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2024-05-25.
- [Simulation of Graph Algorithms with Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01107): Proves by construction that a looped transformer with extra graph-reading attention heads simulates BFS, DFS, Dijkstra and Kosaraju's algorithm with parameters independent of graph size, within finite-precision limits, and is Turing complete at constant width. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-02-02.
- [Looped Transformers are Better at Learning Learning Algorithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12424): Trains a looped transformer with input injection to solve in-context data-fitting problems such as linear regression; it performs comparably to a standard transformer while using less than 10% of the parameters. Category: theory; focus: core; 2023-11-21.
- [CoTFormer: A Chain-of-Thought Driven Architecture with Budget-Adaptive Computation Cost at Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10845): CoTFormer re-applies the same layers several times and lets each pass attend to tokens from earlier passes, like chain-of-thought; it approaches much larger models, and a token-wise adaptive-depth variant cuts compute without losing accuracy. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2023-10-16.
- [Sparse Universal Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.07096): Adds sparse mixture-of-experts and stick-breaking dynamic halting to the Universal Transformer, matching strong baselines on WMT'14 with half the computation and parameters; halting saves around 50% inference computation on formal language tasks with little loss. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2023-10-11.
- [Looped Transformers as Programmable Computers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.13196): Shows that a looped 13-layer transformer with programmed weights, reading instructions and memory from its input, emulates a small instruction-set computer and runs a calculator, linear algebra routines and in-context learning algorithms. Category: theory; focus: core; 2023-01-30.
- [Path Independent Equilibrium Models Can Better Exploit Test-Time Computation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09961): In equilibrium models, upward generalization to harder instances with more test-time iterations correlates with path independence (reaching the same fixed point from any initialization); promoting it improves generalization and penalizing it degrades it. Category: applications; focus: related; 2022-11-18.
- [End-to-end Algorithm Synthesis with Recurrent Networks: Logical Extrapolation Without Overthinking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.05826): Adds recall, which feeds the input into every iteration of a recurrent block, and a progressive loss over random iteration counts; together they prevent overthinking and let networks trained on small problems solve larger ones. Category: applications; focus: related; 2022-02-11.
- [Sliced Recursive Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.05297): SReT shares weights across depth in vision transformers by looping each block; naive recursion gives a ~2% gain, and sliced group self-attention across recursions cuts the added cost by 10~30% with minimal performance loss. Category: applications; focus: related; 2021-11-09.
- [Semantic Communication with Adaptive Universal Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09119): Uses Universal Transformers with adaptive computation time halting as encoder and decoder of a semantic communication system; it reports higher BLEU and lower symbol error ratio than a fixed-depth Transformer system on noisy channels. Category: applications; focus: related; 2021-08-20.
- [PonderNet: Learning to Ponder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.05407): PonderNet runs a step function recurrently with a learned probabilistic halting policy; it outperforms earlier adaptive-computation methods on parity, succeeds at extrapolation, and matches state-of-the-art bAbI accuracy with less compute. Category: depth; focus: related; 2021-07-12.
- [Can You Learn an Algorithm? Generalizing from Easy to Hard Problems with Recurrent Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.04537): Trains weight-tied recurrent networks with few iterations on easy prefix-sum, maze and chess problems and shows that running extra iterations at test time lets them solve harder instances. Category: applications; focus: related; 2021-06-08.
- [Perceiver: General Perception with Iterative Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03206): Perceiver repeatedly cross-attends from a small latent array to large inputs, with weights shared across repeats after the first, like an RNN unrolled in depth; it is competitive across images, point clouds, audio and video. Category: applications; focus: related; 2021-03-04.
- [On the Theory of Implicit Deep Learning: Global Convergence with Implicit Layers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.07346): For deep equilibrium models with nonlinearity only on weights, proves that gradient dynamics reach a global optimum at a linear rate without width assumptions, and relates them to trust region Newton on a shallow layer. Category: theory; focus: related; 2021-02-15.
- [Subformer: Exploring Weight Sharing for Parameter Efficiency in Generative Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.00234): Subformer shares parameters across the central layers of generative Transformers, with unshared first and last layers and self-attentive factorized embeddings; it can beat the Transformer on translation, summarization and language modeling with fewer parameters. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2021-01-01.
- [Multiscale Deep Equilibrium Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08656): MDEQ solves for and backpropagates through the equilibrium points of several feature resolutions at once, using implicit differentiation with O(1) memory; on ImageNet classification and Cityscapes segmentation it matches or exceeds competitive vision models. Category: applications; focus: related; 2020-06-15.
- [Monotone operator equilibrium networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08591): Introduces monDEQ, an implicit-depth model built on monotone operator theory whose parameterization guarantees a unique equilibrium, solved with operator-splitting methods that converge stably; it outperforms Neural ODE-based models while being more computationally efficient. Category: theory; focus: related; 2020-06-15.
- [RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12039): RAFT builds all-pairs 4D correlation volumes and iteratively updates a flow field with a weight-tied recurrent update operator; it reaches 5.10% F1-all error on KITTI and 2.855 pixels end-point error on Sintel (final pass). Category: applications; focus: related; 2020-03-26.
- [Addressing Some Limitations of Transformers with Feedback Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.09402): Feedback Transformer makes every layer attend to per-timestep memory vectors that mix all layers' past representations, exposing high-level past states to low layers; small, shallow models beat comparable Transformers on language modeling, translation and RL. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2020-02-21.
- [Neural Execution of Graph Algorithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10593): Trains graph neural networks to imitate each step of classical graph algorithms by repeating an encode-process-decode network with a learned termination network; max-based message passing works best, and learning reachability alongside improves shortest-path learning. Category: applications; focus: related; 2019-10-23.
- [ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11942): ALBERT reduces BERT's parameters with a factorized embedding and cross-layer parameter sharing, adds an inter-sentence coherence loss, and sets new state-of-the-art results on GLUE, RACE and SQuAD with fewer parameters than BERT-large. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2019-09-26.
- [Deep Equilibrium Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.01377): DEQ finds the fixed point of a weight-tied layer by root-finding and backpropagates through it implicitly; on language modeling such as WikiText-103 it often beats similar-size models while cutting memory by up to 88%. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2019-09-03.
- [Recurrent Stacking of Layers for Compact Neural Machine Translation Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.05353): Shares parameters across all layers of an NMT encoder and decoder; a single layer recurrently stacked 6 times translates comparably to 6 separate layers, and back-translated data improves it further. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2018-07-14.
- [Universal Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03819): Universal Transformer applies the same Transformer block recurrently over depth, with dynamic per-position halting; it is Turing-complete under some assumptions and outperforms standard Transformers on algorithmic and language tasks, gaining 0.9 BLEU on WMT14 En-De. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2018-07-10.
- [Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.08983): Introduces Adaptive Computation Time, a differentiable halting mechanism that lets an RNN learn how many steps to take per input; it improves performance on four synthetic tasks, while gains on character-level language modelling are small. Category: depth; focus: related; 2016-03-29.
- [Neural GPUs Learn Algorithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.08228): The Neural GPU repeats shared convolutional GRU layers for n steps on length-n inputs; trained with parameter sharing relaxation on up to 20-bit numbers, it adds and multiplies much longer binary numbers without errors. Category: applications; focus: related; 2015-11-25.
- [Deeply-Recursive Convolutional Network for Image Super-Resolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.04491): DRCN applies a single convolutional layer recursively, up to 16 recursions, for image super-resolution, adding depth without new parameters; recursive-supervision and skip-connection ease training, and it outperforms previous methods. Category: applications; focus: related; 2015-11-14.

## Open questions

- [Does running more passes at test time than in training keep improving quality?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#extra-passes-at-test-time): mixed; Models trained with a sampled or variable number of passes stay flat or improve slightly beyond the training depth, and their gains level off near the training mean. Ouro, trained with 4 steps and learned exits rather than sampled depth, loses accuracy at 5-8 steps. No source trains the same model both ways, so the role of sampled-depth training is not isolated.
- [Where in the stack should the loop sit?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#loop-placement): consistent; Every comparison favors looping lower or middle layers over the whole stack or the top layers, and in layouts with a shared global KV the loop should include the layers that produce it. The comparisons come from models of 1.3B parameters or less, or from runs whose sizes are not given.
- [With training compute held fixed, do more passes help?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#more-passes-fixed-compute): mixed; On language modeling at the budgets tested, SMELT and MoR find two passes better than three or four with FLOPs fixed, and in Ouro the gap to untied models of the same executed depth grows with the step count. Other results point the other way: Parcae's compute-optimal number of passes rises with the training budget, deeper training recurrence pays off per training FLOP for two of three retrofitted model families, and on Ouro's synthetic Mano task more passes of fewer layers win at the same executed depth.
- [Can later passes reuse one KV cache instead of keeping KV for every pass?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#shared-kv-across-passes): mixed; Reusing the last pass's KV works when the model is trained for it or when it is done only during decoding, while reusing the first pass's KV alone costs accuracy unless a local window is added. Looped CED loses nothing with last-round KV under sampled-depth training but fails with fixed depth, Ouro keeps quality with last-step KV in decoding but not in prefill, and PLT needs a gated sliding window on top of first-pass KV sharing.

## Open models

- [Huginn-0125](https://huggingface.co/tomg-group-umd/huginn-0125): paper 2502.05171; 3.5B params; 800B training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Inkling 2 Mini](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini): paper tml-inkling-2-mini; 26.4B params; not stated training tokens; passes 3; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Ouro-1.4B](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance/Ouro-1.4B): paper 2510.25741; 1.4B params; 7.7T training tokens; passes 4; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Ouro-2.6B](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance/Ouro-2.6B): paper 2510.25741; 2.6B params; 7.7T training tokens; passes 4; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Parcae](https://huggingface.co/SandyResearch/parcae-140m): paper 2604.12946; 140M / 370M / 770M / 1.3B params; 11.2B / 29.6B / 61.6B / 104B training tokens; passes 8; KV per-pass; license not stated on the model cards.
- [Recurrent-Llama-3.2 (4,6,4)](https://huggingface.co/smcleish/Recurrent-Llama-3.2-train-recurrence-4): paper 2511.07384; 851,501,056 excluding embeddings (Table 8) params; about 50B (Nemotron-CC-Math-v1) training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Recurrent-OLMo-2-0425 (4,6,4)](https://huggingface.co/smcleish/Recurrent-OLMo-2-0425-train-recurrence-4): paper 2511.07384; 939,638,784 excluding embeddings (Table 8) params; about 50B (Nemotron-CC-Math-v1-4plus) training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Recurrent-TinyLlama-3T (4,8,4)](https://huggingface.co/smcleish/Recurrent-TinyLlama-3T-train-recurrence-4): paper 2511.07384; 704,708,608 excluding embeddings (Table 8) params; about 50B (train-recurrence-k repos); 26B single phase, 52B two phase training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [TML-d24-varloop-research](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research): paper tml-inkling-2-mini; 26.4B params; not stated training tokens; passes 3; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
